operative_quote: I declare that section 29 of the Kenya Information and Communication Act is unconstitutional
source_paragraph: Disposition, order (a) (source has no paragraph numbers)
case_name: Andare v Attorney General & another; Article 19 – East Africa (Interested Party) [2016] KEHC 7592 (KLR)
notes: Whole section. Reasoning (Disposition) also finds s.29 'null and void' for violating Art 33. Court declined to find Art 50(2)(n) violation. DPP barred from continuing prosecution under s.29 (last para).

scope_text: to the extent that it covers offences other than those contemplated under Article 33 (2) (a)- (d ) of the Constitution of Kenya 2010
operative_quote: A declaration be and is hereby issued that section 194 of the Penal Code, cap 63, Laws of Kenya is unconstitutional and invalid to the extent that it covers offences other than those contemplated under Article 33 (2) (a)- (d ) of the Constitution of Kenya 2010
source_paragraph: Final orders, declaration (i) (source has no paragraph numbers; bracketed numbers are footnote markers)
case_name: Jacqueline Okuta & another v Attorney General & 2 others [2017] KEHC 8382 (KLR)
notes: Order is partial, but the reasoning condemns criminal defamation wholesale ('it is absolutely unnecessary to criminalize defamatory statements'). Source header reads PETITION NO. 397 OF 2016, not 2015.
flag: ambiguous: order partial vs reasoning total

scope_text: to the extent that it provides for the mandatory death sentence for murder
operative_quote: The mandatory nature of the death sentence as provided for under section 204 of the Penal Code is hereby declared unconstitutional.
case_name: Muruatetu & another v Republic; Katiba Institute & 5 others (Amicus Curiae) [2017] KESC 2 (KLR)
notes: Order 112(a) continues: 'this order does not disturb the validity of the death sentence as contemplated under article 26(3)'. Para 69: death penalty 'still applicable as a discretionary maximum punishment'. Para 52 affirms CA in Mutiso; Mwaura (CA) effectively displaced but not expressly overruled in text.

scope_text: apply only in respect to sentences of murder under sections 203 and 204 of the Penal Code
operative_quote: The decision of Muruatetu and these guidelines apply only in respect to sentences of murder under sections 203 and 204 of the Penal Code
case_name: Muruatetu & another v Republic; Katiba Institute & 5 others (Amicus Curiae) [2021] KESC 31 (KLR)
notes: Directions limit the reach of B03, do not change s.204's status. Para 11: Muruatetu 'did not invalidate mandatory sentences or minimum sentences in the Penal Code, the Sexual Offences Act or any other statute'. Para 15: ss.40(3), 296(2), 297(2) must be challenged separately; 'Muruatetu as it now stands cannot directly be applicable to those cases.'

operative_quote: A declaration is hereby issued that Section 132 of the Penal Code is unconstitutional and invalid.
case_name: Robert Alai v The Hon Attorney General & another [2017] KEHC 6090 (KLR)
notes: Formal order is total. Para 61 reasoning is qualified: inconsistent 'in so far as it suppresses freedom of expression, shifts burden to an accused, denies an accused the right to remain silent and derogates the right to fair hearing'.
flag: ambiguous: order total vs 'in so far as' reasoning

operative_quote: A declaration is hereby issued that section 66 of the Penal Code is unconstitutional and invalid for unjustifiably violating articles 33 and 50(2)(a) of the Constitution
case_name: Andama v Director of Public Prosecutions & 2 others; Article 19 East Africa (Interested Party) [2021] KEHC 12538 (KLR)
notes: Covers s.66(1) offence and s.66(2) reverse-onus defence (paras 46-49).

operative_quote: we are not satisfied that the Petitioners’ attack on the constitutional validity of sections 162 and 165 of the Penal Code is sustainable. We find that the impugned sections are not unconstitutional.

notes: Challenge framed against s.162(a) and (c) only (paras 1, 242); s.162(b) (animals) never challenged. Dispositive para 406 speaks of 'sections 162 and 165'. Three-judge bench.

scope_text: so as not to take away the discretion of the court in sentencing
operative_quote: we hold that the provisions of section 8 of the sexual Offences Act must be interpreted so as not to take away the discretion of the court in sentencing
notes: No declaration of unconstitutionality. Para 38 applies Muruatetu reasoning to SOA. Applies to s.8 generally (8(2)-(4)); conviction was under 8(3). Internal inconsistency: para 41 says 10 years adequate, para 42 substitutes 15 years.

scope_text: the mandatory nature of the sentences provided for in the SOA
operative_quote: we believe that the same, as applies to the unconstitutionality of mandatory sentences, can be applied mutatis mutandis to the mandatory nature of the sentences provided for in the SOA
notes: No formal declaration and no section number in the holding; orders (35) only substitute sentence. Para 32: mandatory sentences 'conflicts with the principle of separation of powers'. SC in kesc/2024/34 para 64 calls this a 'declaration of unconstitutionality' but para 65 says CA 'did not declare any particular provision ... unconstitutional'.

operative_quote: The Petition of Appeal is allowed to the extent of setting aside the Judgment of the Court of Appeal in Nyeri in Criminal Appeal No 84 of 2015 Joshua Gichuki Mwangi v Republic delivered on October 7, 2022.
case_name: Republic v Mwangi; Initiative for Strategic Litigation in Africa (ISLA) & 3 others (Amicus Curiae) [2024] KESC 34 (KLR)
notes: SC did NOT declare s.8 constitutional: para 69 'lawful and remains lawful as long as section 8 of the Sexual Offences Act remains valid'; para 63 constitutionality of minimum sentences must be filed in HC first. Not an 'upheld' event.

scope_text: the imposition of a mandatory indeterminate life sentence
operative_quote: having found the sentence of life imprisonment to be unconstitutional, we have the discretion to interfere with the said sentence
notes: Targets s.8(2) (life for child 11 or under; ground c, para 5). Finding is in reasoning, not in formal orders (27 only substitutes 40 years). Reasoning (21) is about life sentences generally, not tied to s.8(2) text.
flag: ambiguous: declared_unconstitutional vs interpreted; provision-level target unclear

operative_quote: The life imprisonment sentence imposed by the trial court and affirmed by the High Court is hereby reinstated.
notes: Para 66: CA 'violated the principle of stare decisis by misapplying the decision in Muruatetu and in finding the life sentences of imprisonment to be unconstitutional.' Para 55: SC itself does not decide constitutionality of life imprisonment.

scope_text: to the extent that it determined the parameters of life imprisonment
operative_quote: the remedy that commends itself to us, is the setting aside of the Court of Appeal’s Judgment to the extent that it determined the parameters of life imprisonment
notes: Reverses CA Ayako v Republic, Criminal Appeal 22 of 2018 (8 Dec 2023), which held life imprisonment cruel and set 30 years (paras 13-18). That CA judgment is not in the dataset, so affects_event is empty. Para 41: SC does not decide constitutionality of life imprisonment.
